newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate passes airports sale bill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate passes airports sale bill.

text.p: The Australian upper house of parliament, the Senate, on Thursday approved the A$2 billion sale of Australia's airports.
The Senate made a number of amendments to the bill, the most significant being a government-sponsored change to include Perth airport in the cross-ownership provisions.
Under the amended cross-ownership provisions, anyone who holds a controlling stake in the main Sydney airports is limited to a 15 percent holding in those at Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth.

The government was satisfied with the changes and expected the sell-off legislation to soon win final approval in the lower house, a spokesman told Reuters. "It goes back to the House of Representatives now and we're hopeful it will pass," he said.
Perth's inclusion in the cross-ownership measures followed a request from the Western Australian state government, the spokesman said.

The two Greens senators, backed by other non-government parties, forced some minor changes to the bill, including a requirement to supply an airport development plan whenever a development was likely to have an impact on the environment.
The government plans to raise about A$2 billion through the long-term leasing of the Federal Airports Corp's 23 airports.
Once the legislation is passed, the airports' 50-year leases will be thrown open to bids.

Interested groups currently include a consortium comprising transport group Brambles Industries Ltd, financial services group Lend Lease Corp Ltd and Irish government-owned airports authority Aer Rianta.
